record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Describe/classify the collections of algebraically indep endent homogeneous polynomials σ1,..., σn, deg σk = k, in n variables x1,..., xn with the required property. Finally, one question revealing the relationship between singularities o f bi-Hamiltonian systems and singular points of Nijenhuis operators. In a recent paper [31], it was shown that the structure of singularities of bi-Hamiltonian systems related to Poisson pencils of Kr onecker type is determined by the singularities of the pencil. We expect that a similar principle works f or Poisson pencils of sympletic type, i.e., when one of two compatible Poisson brackets is non-degen erate. In this case, we have a well-defined recursion operator R (which is automatically a Nijenhuis operator) and the commuting 31 functions we are interested in are just the coefficients σ1,..., σn of the characteristic polynomial of R. We assume that they are independent almost everywhere on M and want to study singular points of the mapping Phi = ( σ1,..., σn): M → Rn playing the role of the momentum mapping for our bi-Hamiltonian system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth $2n$-dimensional manifold endowed with two compatible Poisson brackets $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_0$ and $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_1$ (i.e., every linear combination $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_0+\lambda\{\cdot,\cdot\}_1$ is again a Poisson bracket) such that $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_0$ is non-degenerate. The corresponding recursion operator $R:TM\to TM$, defined by $\{f,g\}_1=\{f,R\,dg\}_0$ (equivalently $R=P_1 P_0^{-1}$ where $P_i$ are the Poisson tensors), is then a Nijenhuis operator. Let $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n$ denote the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of $R$ (so $\det(tI-R)=(t^n-\sigma_1 t^{n-1}+\sigma_2 t^{n-2}-\dots)^2$ after taking the square root in the symplectic case, with $\sigma_k$ a smooth function on $M$). Assume these functions are functionally independent almost everywhere and pairwise Poisson-commute, so that $\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ serves as the momentum map of the resulting bi-Hamiltonian integrable system.

Consider the linearization of this setup at a singular point: at such a point one obtains, after a suitable choice of coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_n$, a collection of algebraically independent homogeneous polynomials $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with $\deg\sigma_k=k$ that pairwise commute with respect to a constant Poisson structure and arise as the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a linear Nijenhuis operator.

Problem. Describe and classify all such collections $(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ of algebraically independent homogeneous polynomials with $\deg\sigma_k=k$ in $n$ variables having this property, and use the classification to describe the singular points of the momentum map $\Phi=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ of a bi-Hamiltonian system of symplectic (i.e., non-degenerate) type in terms of the singularities of the underlying Poisson pencil / Nijenhuis operator.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2018 collection of open problems on finite-dimensional integrable systems and has motivated subsequent work on Nijenhuis/left-symmetric algebras (e.g. arXiv:2404.11282 classifies differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis structures in low dimension), but no general classification of the collections $(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ in arbitrary dimension or a complete description of singularities for symplectic-type Poisson pencils has been established. The problem appears to remain open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems, Questions, and Challenges in Finite-Dimensional Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 5.16 asks to describe/classify the collections of algebraically independent homogeneous polynomials σ1,...,σn with deg σk = k arising from Nijenhuis recursion operators of symplectic-type Poisson pencils.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in the 2018 collection.

status_evidence.title: Classification of differentially non-degenerate Nijenhuis structures (arXiv:2404.11282)
status_evidence.snippet: Partial classification results for low-dimensional Nijenhuis/left-symmetric algebras related to the program initiated by Bolsinov et al.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists in low dimensions but a general classification is not given.
